ImageDescription.value: The Anzeiger-Hochhaus in Hanover is a 51-metre-tall high-rise building constructed between 1927 and 1928 near Steintorplatz. Built as the publishing headquarters of the Hannoverscher Anzeiger, it is recognised for its 12-metre-high green dome, a well-known landmark of the city. The building is one of the few major representative structures in Hanover to have survived the bombing raids of the Second World War almost unscathed.

ImageDescription.value: This photo frames Humayun’s Tomb through a narrow water channel, emphasizing its perfect symmetry and mirrored reflection. Warm red sandstone contrasts with the white marble dome under a soft sky, and the low-angle view makes the monument feel grand. In the foreground three pigeons bring the scene to life — the middle pigeon is drinking from the channel while the other two stand to its left and right, adding scale and a natural focal point that draws the eye into the composition.

ImageDescription.value: The Wrede passage (Finnish: Wreden pasaasi. Swedish: Wredes passage; also known as the "Old merchant alley", Finnish: Vanha kauppakuja, or the "Grandma tunnel", Finnish: Mummotunneli) is an entity formed by two stone buildings in Kluuvi, Helsinki, Finland. The name refers also to the merchant alley stretching throughout the block. The passage is formed by the Wrede house in the corner between Pohjoisesplanadi and Mikonkatu (Pohjoisesplanadi 35) and the Central house in the corner between Aleksanterinkatu and Mikonkatu (Aleksanterinkatu 46). The building entity represents Renaissance Revival architecture and was designed and partly commissioned by architect Karl August Wrede, and built in 1888 and 1892.
